HOW IT WORKS
Log a want the day you feel it: the name, the price and the date. The file starts a 30-day clock. When you notice you no longer want it, you fill Dropped On. If you buy it, you fill Bought On. If day 30 comes and you still want it, you fill Rechecked On and a second clock starts. Everything else is worked out for you.

In the sample data, 23 wishes have run out their 30 days. 19 of them died on their own, with a median of 11 days. Together they cost $3,154 you did not spend. Only 4 survived, and the file shows you exactly which ones.

WHAT IS INSIDE (5 PAGES)
00 NO BUY YEAR. The hub. Your numbers at a glance, the decisions due this week, the four pages and a three-note first week: Today, This week, On day 30.
01 Wishes. The only page where you type. One table with five tabs: Open, Past 30 Days, Survived, Died and All Wishes. Properties you fill: Wish, Added On, Price, Category (8 options), Dropped On, Bought On, Rechecked On, Notes.
02 Dropout. How many wants died on their own, the median days they lasted, the dollars you did not spend, two bar charts by category, the survivors, and the wants you bought before day 30.
03 This Month. Wants added, wants that died, dollars kept and clocks that run out this month, with the list of each.
04 Settings and Help. A Show Demo switch, an As Of date, the maths in plain words, a diagram of how the clock works and a short FAQ.

THE NUMBERS
5 pages, 1 table you type in, 56 sample wishes, 25 formulas, 29 views, 17 charts and number tiles. Every figure comes from the dates you type. Nothing is estimated.

THREE OUTCOMES, ONE RULE
Waiting while the clock runs. Died when you drop it. Bought when you buy it. Still open when it survives 30 days and you have not decided. A want that survives two full clocks is flagged as a Real Want, so you know which purchases are worth making.

TWO THINGS YOU DID NOT EXPECT
Real Wants: the file flags the wants that survived two clocks. Bought before day 30: a separate list of purchases made inside the 30 days, with your note beside each. Not every early purchase is a slip, and the list lets you judge.

WHO IT IS FOR
Anyone starting a no buy year or a no spend month, especially in January, who has already kept a wish list and dropped it because nothing ever came out of it.

WHAT IT DOES NOT DO
It does not connect to your bank, import transactions or track what you spend. It is not a budget. It does not send reminders. It does not tell you whether you need something. It counts wishes, dates and prices you type in. The dropout numbers need wishes whose 30 days are up, so they read zero until your first clocks run out.

WHAT YOU NEED
A Notion account. A free account is enough to duplicate it. The tiles and bar charts are Notion charts, and some plans limit how many charts show. If yours does, every figure also reads from the tabs on page 01. Everything inside is in English.

After your order you receive a PDF with your link. Open it, click Duplicate at the top right, choose your workspace. The 56 sample wishes are there so you can see every page working. Untick Show Demo in Settings and they all disappear.

No. A free account can duplicate it. Charts are limited by Notion on some plans; every figure also reads from the tabs on page 01.

Can I edit it?
Yes. Every property, view and page is yours once you duplicate it.

Untick Show Demo in Settings and all 56 vanish from every page.

Open it in the Notion app. It was built and checked on desktop, so wide columns may stack on a narrow screen.
